name: LIS Technologies
about: LIS Technologies (Laser Isotope Separation Technologies) is commercializing CRISLA, a laser uranium enrichment process that uses 5.3-micron infrared lasers, to produce low-enriched uranium for large reactors and high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) for small and micro reactors. Based in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Selected by DOE in 2024 as one of six participants in its LEU enrichment acquisition program. Plans a commercial laser enrichment facility at the K-25 site in Oak Ridge. Filed a letter of intent with the NRC for a license application in March 2026.
expected_reason: Enrichment for the same DOE and reactor buyers as General Matter, Centrus, Urenco and GLE.

name: FluxPoint Energy
about: FluxPoint Energy, based in Houston and McLean, Virginia, plans what it expects to be the first new US uranium conversion plant in more than 70 years, in Texas: converting uranium oxide into uranium hexafluoride (UF6), the feedstock that enrichment plants process into reactor fuel. Filed a uranium conversion facility letter of intent with the NRC in April 2026.
expected_reason: Conversion produces the UF6 that enrichers like General Matter buy.

name: Curio
about: Curio is developing NuCycle, a used nuclear fuel recycling production facility, and in May 2026 asked the NRC to open a 10 CFR Part 70 docket for pre-application work toward an operating license. Engineering design is underway with Sargent & Lundy; the site had not been chosen as of May 2026.
expected_reason: Unclear: recycled fuel competes at the margin with enriched fuel; no incumbent in the map recycles at commercial scale.

name: Thorium Atomics
about: Thorium Atomics, based in Knoxville, Tennessee, is developing a thorium-fueled gas-cooled reactor of about 250 MWth. It met NRC staff in May 2026 and filed a letter of intent in June 2026 to begin pre-application licensing activities; it has also met Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission staff.
expected_reason: A gas-cooled reactor competes with X-energy's and Kairos's advanced reactors for the same utility and industrial buyers.

name: Firestorm Labs
about: Firestorm Labs, based in San Diego, builds Group 2 drones such as the Tempest (under 55 lb, 7-foot wingspan, up to 10 lb payload) and xCell, a drone factory packed into two shipping containers that 3D-prints airframes near the front line, up to 50 drones a month per unit. Holds a $100 million US Air Force contract covering drone delivery, support and R&D. Registered dozens of airframes with the FAA since September 2025.
expected_reason: Sells small military drones to the same buyers as Anduril, Shield AI and AeroVironment.
